sections.h2: What should I know about Shelbyville before selling a house there?
sections.html:
Shelbyville is the seat of Bedford County, laid out in 1810 and incorporated in 1819, on a limestone bluff of the Highland Rim where the Duck River curls around the south and east sides of town. It covers about 18.4 square miles, and US 231 meets US 41A in town. The city is nicknamed the Walking Horse Capital of the World and the Pencil City, and the Tennessee Walking Horse National Celebration fills the 11 days before Labor Day each year.

The Census Bureau estimates 26,146 residents as of July 1, 2025, which is 11.1% above the April 2020 base and well above the 20,335 counted in 2010. Manufacturing and distribution anchor the local economy, with Musgrave Pencil, a Tyson facility, a Walmart distribution center and several trucking firms among the employers Wikipedia names. Those jobs, plus a county seat's courts and offices, shape who buys here.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers tell a Shelbyville seller?
sections.html:
Shelbyville's median owner-occupied value is $244,000 for 2020 to 2024, the lowest among these four Tennessee cities, and just 50.7% of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $1,056. The 9,089 households average 2.64 people, and 28.4% of residents are under 18, so family houses with several bedrooms are a core product.

  • Median household income: $55,073 in 2024 dollars
  • Persons in poverty: 20.7%
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 13.1%
  • Mean commute: 27.2 minutes

With half the housing rented, investor-owned houses and small rental properties turn over regularly. Details are on Census QuickFacts for Shelbyville.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 reappraisal change Bedford County tax rates?
sections.html:
On June 30, 2026 the county commission approved $198 million in budgets and held the property tax at the state's certified rate. Bedford County was in a reappraisal year, and most owners received higher appraisals. The old rate of $2.3252 per $100 of assessed value dropped to the certified $1.5083, so the average owner should see little change in the bill unless a value rose faster than the county average.

At 25% residential assessment, a house at the Census median of $244,000 is assessed at $61,000, which gives about $920 in county tax at the new rate before any city levy. Source: the county's budget announcement.

sections.h2: Does Shelbyville have its own property tax bill?
sections.html:
Yes. The city takes payment for its levy separately from the county. Pay online or by phone through a third-party processor that adds a fee, by mail to the City of Shelbyville, P.O. Box 185, Shelbyville, TN 37162, or in person at City Hall, 201 North Spring Street on the Public Square. Include the top stub and write the receipt number on a mailed check.

Ask the city for the current-year city rate, since the county announcement covers only the county portion. The state schedule says current-year tax is due on the first Monday in October, and the last day to pay the prior year's tax without interest is February 28. Because two jurisdictions bill separately, a seller should ask the title company to pull both statements before closing.

sections.h2: Is there tax relief for older or disabled owners in Bedford County?
sections.html:
The Comptroller's list sets Bedford County's freeze income limit at $43,780 for tax year 2026, close to the state's $38,470 minimum. Application deadlines fall 35 days after the delinquency date, which lands in April. Disabled veterans and low-income elderly or disabled owners have separate relief programs run through the county trustee.

A freeze locks the tax at the first qualifying year's amount, so tell your buyer's side if your house carries one. It is also worth checking whether a greenbelt classification applies to a larger lot, because the state's application deadline for greenbelt is March 15.

sections.h2: What permits and zoning rules affect a Shelbyville sale?
sections.html:
The Building and Codes Department, at (931) 488-4230, requires a permit to build, enlarge, alter, repair, move or demolish a structure, and also for pools, decks, arbors and storage buildings. Permits and applications now run only through the city's OpenGov portal, and some residential, fence, sign, accessory structure and driveway applications are online only. The department enforces the 2018 International Codes, and simple permits can be issued the same day.

If a buyer wants a different zoning, the process runs through the Planning Department, a pre-planning meeting, the Planning Commission and two City Council readings, and the ordinance takes effect 15 days after the public hearing. A sale usually does not need a rezoning, but confirm the current zone before you promise a buyer a use such as a duplex or a home business.

  • Call before you start any repair that changes structure or systems.
  • Keep permit finals with your closing documents.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded at the Bedford County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Register records documents that give public notice of ownership, liens and contracts, and reports the state's conveyance and mortgage taxes to the Department of Revenue each month. The office has an online fee calculator for any filing, and a free fraud alert service that emails you when a document is recorded under your name. Statewide, the transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of price and the mortgage tax is $0.115 per $100 of debt after the first $2,000.

For a house at the Census median of $244,000, the transfer tax comes to $902.80. The buyer's title company will usually file, but your contract should state who covers it.

sections.h2: What does Shelbyville's setting mean for an older house?
sections.html:
Shelbyville gets about 59.4 inches of rain a year and roughly 128 days with measurable precipitation, and snow is rare at about an inch. Summer highs average near 89 degrees in July, with a recorded top of 108. That much moisture makes roofs, crawl spaces and drainage the first things a buyer's inspector tends to check.

Bedford County School District runs the public schools, and Shelbyville Central High School is the local high school. A house's attendance zone is set by the district, so ask the district office instead of relying on a listing site.

sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a house in Shelbyville?
sections.html:
A traditional listing gives the widest exposure, but the pool of buyers who can finance near the $244,000 median may be narrower than in Nashville's suburbs. A cash buyer who accepts the house as-is, with tenants or deferred repairs, can close on the timeline title work allows.

Compare any cash figure with your likely net after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Ask for it in writing, settle the county and city tax statements, and let a title company record the deed.

faqs.q: What is the Bedford County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county commission adopted the state's certified rate of $1.5083 per $100 of assessed value on June 30, 2026, down from $2.3252 the year before. City tax is billed separately.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Shelbyville city property tax?
faqs.a: At City Hall, 201 North Spring Street, by mail to P.O. Box 185, online, or by phone at 1-866-414-2699. Online and phone payments carry a third-party fee.

faqs.q: Can I get a permit for a fence or accessory building in Shelbyville?
faqs.a: Yes, through the city's OpenGov portal. Fence, accessory structure, sign and driveway applications are online only. Call (931) 488-4230 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax on a Shelbyville sale?
faqs.a: Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 of price. A $244,000 house therefore owes $902.80 at recording, and the contract decides which party pays.

faqs.q: What is the freeze income limit for Bedford County?
faqs.a: For tax year 2026 the Comptroller lists $43,780. Applicants must be 65 or older and meet the program's ownership and residence rules.
